title: Session Symphony — turn orchestration prototype sketch
content:
Overview:
This is a messy personal sketch for a lightweight feature I'm calling 'Session Symphony' — an orchestration layer that treats a user session as a small orchestra of signals (turns, context, signals) and dynamically composes per-turn execution plans to hit latency/cost/quality targets.

Why:
- We keep tweaking per-request routing, fidelity lanes, and ad-hoc fallbacks. For many assistant-style apps the right decisions are session-dependent (user priority, history length, hallucination sensitivity, downstream cost budget).
- Instead of per-request ad-hoc rules, bundle session-level intent and QoS signals and let a small planner pick strategies for the next N turns.

High-level sketch (proto):
- SessionProfile: small JSON that contains: priority (low/normal/high), budget (tokens per minute or $), fidelity hints (compressible, exactness-sensitive), allowed-model-classes, allowed-quantizations, sticky-kv-policy.
- TurnPlan: for each turn the planner emits: model-choice, temperature/decoding, prefix-kv-check (use cached prefix? yes/no), mode (fast/normal/precise), fallback-policy (use smaller model if latency > X), enrichment-hooks (run reranker post-hypothesis?).
- Rolling window: planner recalculates every M tokens or on explicit signal (user switches to workspace mode).

Rough user stories (for proto scope):
1) As a product engineer, I want sessions with "high" priority to prefer lower-latency model variants so that user-facing chat stays snappy.
2) As an analytics engineer, I want sessions with an explicit cost budget to throttle fidelity (shorter context, more token trimming) before switching to paid fallback.
3) As an ML engineer, I want to test canaries where the planner routes 10% of sessions to a new quantized model and collects quality/latency metrics.
4) As a researcher, I want to set a knob that marks some sessions as "exactness-sensitive" so we avoid aggressive compression or prompting shortcuts.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- A SessionProfile protobuf/JSON is persisted at session start and readable by runtime routing.
- A lightweight planner service (or function) takes SessionProfile + recent telemetry and returns a TurnPlan in <50ms median.
- Serving runtime executes TurnPlan fields (model selection, kv usage flag, decoding params).
- Telemetry: per-session logs capture planner decisions and resulting latency/cost/quality metrics for evaluation.

Operational considerations:
- Planner must be cheap and replicated; ideally colocated with ingress to avoid extra hop latency.
- TurnPlan must be fail-closed: if planner is unreachable, runtime uses a conservative default (normal fidelity, low-cost model).
- Backwards compatibility: existing API calls that don't submit a SessionProfile should get a default session (priority=normal, budget=off).
- Security: session profile may contain PII? keep minimal; prefer opaque role-tags rather than free text.

Prototype timeline (2-phase):
Phase A (3 sprints) - Prove concept in hosted path:
- Sprint 1: SessionProfile schema + API extension (optional header + session create endpoint) + simple planner that picks model by priority.
- Sprint 2: Integrate TurnPlan into runtime (model selection flag + kv-use toggle) + logging.
- Sprint 3: Run internal canary (10% sessions) + collect metrics + quick eval harness for quality delta.

Phase B (follow-on) - richer policies + UI in Console:
- Policy language for budget consumption rules.
- Console UI to set session policies and inspect decisions.
- Dedicated path/backpressure integration.

Open questions / risks (my notes):
- How big should SessionProfile be? keep it under ~300 bytes to avoid perf penalty in headers.
- Planner TTL vs. recalculation frequency: update on heavy signals (e.g., user switches to "compose longer answer").
- How to version policies across runtime and planner (degraded planner should be able to handle older TurnPlan fields).
- Telemetry volume: logging per-turn plans increases volume; we should sample or batch.
- Interaction with token-level caching: if planner flips kv-use on/off mid-session, need seamless cache invalidation or prefix merge strategy.

Quick implementation notes (dev-to-self):
- Schema: session_profile_v1 {priority:enum, budget_u_tokens:int64 (nullable), fidelity_tags:[str], allowed_models:[str], sticky_kv:bool}
- Planner API sketch: POST /planner/v1/plan {session_profile, last_turns_summary, current_latency_estimate} -> {turn_plan, plan_version, ttl_ms}
- TurnPlan fields minimal: {model_id, decoding_profile_id, use_kv_prefix:true|false, fallback_chain:[model_id], note}

Experiments I'd like to run early:
- Can we reduce mean latency by 10-20% for high-priority sessions by routing to a lower-latency variant while keeping quality > 95% of baseline (evaluate via small eval set)?
- Budget enforcement: compare hard token-throttling vs progressive fidelity shifts (compress summaries, then degrade models). Which yields better UX?

Notes to self / TODOs:
- [ ] Grab Samir's notes on fallback orchestration (ref: linear SY-12?) and fold into policy examples.
- [ ] Build quick eval harness: 500 synthetic sessions across three modalities (faq, creative, step-by-step) and compare decisions.
- [ ] Check with infra whether planner colocated with ingress will be acceptable for hosted path.
- [ ] Mock console page: list of sessions -> view TurnPlan timeline.

Loose sketch of UX strings to use in Console (for later):
- "Session priority: keep latency under 150ms"
- "Budget: $0.10 per minute"
- "Exactness sensitive: do not compress or quantize"

Random design idea (braindump):
- "Concert mode": allow a session owner to pin a sequence of TurnPlans (e.g., for a guided flow) so that decisions are deterministic for the duration of the flow. Useful for tutorials, demos, and tests.

That's it for now. This doc is intentionally fuzzy — I want a short, runnable prototype that buys early telemetry. Next step: wire up a minimal session header and planner stub that picks from 3 model variants and returns TTL=30s.

If you read this and want to riff, leave notes inline or ping me in #prod-hosted-api.

-- diego
user_stories: As an engineer, route high-priority sessions to lower-latency variants.
As a product manager, set per-session dollar budget and have runtime enforce fidelity shifts.
As an SRE, have planner fail-closed defaults and simple observability for decisions.
acceptance_criteria: SessionProfile persisted and readable at request time.
Planner returns TurnPlan in <50ms median for 95% of calls.
Telemetry captures planner decisions and resulting SLO metrics.
